correctness.rationale: Each interior flip toggles two independent Bernoulli boundary variables. Equal boundaries, probability 1/2, shift the run list by two; all but O(1) affected depth-aligned token comparisons equal two-step geometric run-length mismatch indicators, whose mean is exactly 2/3 and whose two-dependence permits a uniform interval strong law. Run density 1/2 and independent uniform edit location yield the exact half-atom/half-Unif[0,1/6] limit, with boundedness yielding mean 1/24. Both token implementations matched all 32,766 binary words at lengths 1–14 and all 360,456 directed interior flips were checked; only the analytic proof certifies the infinite limit.

value.rationale: The original reversible string transform distinguishes localized run-length changes from nonlocal character-edit realignments. The exact random-bit-flip rewrite distribution resolves the natural quantitative stability question for this representation: half asymptotically local events and a nontrivial continuous linear-scale response in the remaining half, providing a mathematically motivated benchmark without claiming token edit distance.
